96c1b9c1c52a:
✨️2 February: The Presentation of the Lord in the Temple

On this great feast day I am showing you an icon with a theme that is rare in Romanian iconography on glass (model: Nicula, second half of the 18th century), an icon that has joined an impressive collection of icons on glass belonging to a lovely Romanian family from Transylvania.

Forty days after His birth, the Saviour's parents performed the ritual of bringing Him to the Temple to redeem Him, as the Law of Moses required.

According to the Law, the Israelites were required to bring every firstborn male to the temple and dedicate him to the Lord, a practice explained by the sparing of the Israelites' firstborn on the night they left Egypt.

The offering was a lamb and a dove. The poor, who had no lamb, could bring two young pigeons (one of which symbolised the offering of thanks to God for the gift received, while the other was the price of redemption for the child, who would otherwise have had to dedicate his life to the service of God).
3e0d7081be4a:
⚜️The Mother of God “the Unfading Flower”, icon on glass

This icon is also called “the Immaculate Flower” or “the Lily Flower”.

The lily symbolises the unfading flower of the virginity and purity of the All-pure Virgin Mary, to whom the Church sings in its hymns: “You are the root of virginity and the unwithering Flower of purity” (doxologia.ro)

The icon is not available; it was ordered as a gift.
a290cd681d69:
12 January: the veneration of the icon «The Mother of God, the Nursing Mother» (Galaktotrophousa, the Nourisher of Life)

One of the oldest such depictions of the Mother of God is on the Holy Mountain of Athos (Hilandar Monastery); other depictions of this theme (as miniatures) can be admired in manuscripts and, of course, many delightful depictions are found in the icons on glass of the Transylvanian masters, one of them (workshop in Șcheii Brașovului, second half of the 19th century) being the model after which we made this icon in our workshop.

The icon is not available; contact me if you would like a depiction on glass of this special theme.
791b28cf7bb5:
6 January: The Baptism of the Lord (Theophany)

The theme of the Baptism of the Lord, one of the great events of Christendom, also called Theophany, Epiphany or the Divine Manifestation, holds an important place in the world of the peasant icons on glass.

Two similar versions of the same theme painted in our workshop (model from Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century) show Jesus Christ in a humble attitude, with His hands crossed on His chest, at the moment He is baptised by His Forerunner, the great prophet John.

Also in a humble attitude is an angel of the Lord, holding a towel in both hands as the Lord comes out of the waters of the Jordan. From the clouds, the Holy Spirit appears in the form of a dove.

Both icons were ordered, so they are not available.
3bcf0cf08f17:
⚜️Saint Nikephoros the Leper, the Wonderworker (4 January)

We welcome the feast of Saint Nikephoros the Leper with an icon on glass ordered for a holy Church in Dobrogea.
The icon shows Saint Nikephoros with scenes from his life (glass 42x30 cm).

A few words about this lesser-known saint (excerpts from «Drepții în veci vor fi vii» – The righteous shall live for ever – by Simon the Monk):

“The Venerable Nikephoros the Leper was born on the island of Crete into a family of devout peasants and was orphaned at an early age. At thirteen, the first signs of the “holy disease”, as leprosy is called in the Church of Christ, appeared on his body. To escape the permanent isolation that awaited him, he took refuge for a time in Egypt.

At twenty-four he arrived at the leper colony on Chios, in the care of Saint Anthimos of Chios, where he was tonsured a monk. There, for forty-one years, although more and more crippled by the disease, he gave himself with a martyr's patience to struggles beyond nature, becoming an example for his brothers in suffering.

After the cure for leprosy was discovered in 1947, the leper colony on Chios was closed and the Venerable one was moved to the Saint Barbara Hospital in Athens. Blind and confined to his sickbed, yet endowed with many divine gifts, he spent the last years of his life giving hope to the despairing, comfort to the suffering and zeal to the young.

At the age of seventy-four the holy leper departed this world; later, the finding of his holy relics and the countless healings he still works today showed him to be one of the greatest intercessors of our times.
In 2012 the Ecumenical Patriarchate glorified Saint Nikephoros the Leper, with his feast on 4 January, the day of his falling asleep.”
16f6e4d77890:
✤ 4 January – «Saint Nikephoros the Leper», a healing and wonderworking saint.

• We welcome the feast of Saint Nikephoros the Leper with an icon on glass ordered for a holy Church in Dobrogea.

Dear friends,

today (the day our workshop turns two) I am showing you one of the first icons I painted (2019): «The Sorrowful Mother of God» (model: Arpașu de Sus, 1877).
It is also my first icon ordered for a holy Church.

In these two years I began receiving orders from you very soon after the workshop opened, and the orders have continued over these years, so that I have had to schedule them for later periods, and the scheduling continues.

Thank you for all the icons I have painted in these two years. Thank you for your patience and understanding in agreeing to wait your turn. Thank you for sharing, commenting on and liking my posts, and so supporting our page, which would not exist without you.

I wish you and your families a new year of achievements, health, peace and joy, and for our workshop, many more beautiful icons painted on glass.

Happy New Year!
8682af476e2d:
✤ The Holy Trinity and the Coronation of the Mother of God

• The scene (an ink drawing) shows the Holy Trinity (the spiritual unity of the three divine persons): Jesus Christ carrying the Cross of the crucifixion, God the Father with the orb and sceptre (the insignia of the Almighty), and the Holy Spirit (as a white dove framed by the sun) sending down His blessing. The first two hold a crown above the head of the Virgin Mary (kneeling, with her hands crossed on her chest). The figures are “held up” by clouds.
